headlines.article_text: Anthropic IPO live updates: ANT stock price and Nasdaq debut Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu watch now VIDEO 4:58 04:58 Anthropic tops $2 trillion market cap in Nasdaq debut: Here’s what experts have to say Rapid Recap Anthropic jumped 17% in its Nasdaq debut on Thursday in a seminal moment for artificial intelligence, after the company completed the biggest initial public offering on record, topping SpaceX' s historic debut in June. The stock closed at $97.17 per share. The Claude creator, trading under the ticker "ANT," opened at $111.50, after the company raised $81.3 billion in the IPO. Anthropic sold 980 million shares at $83 a piece on Wednesday, lifting the size and price of its offering. At Thursday's close, Anthropic had a fully diluted market cap of roughly $1.8 trillion. More than 846 million shares changed hands, surpassing the 522 million shares that were traded on SpaceX's opening day. The 5-year-old company captivated the corporate world with its Claude AI models and products, which have fueled its meteoric rise this year. Anthropic said in its prospectus that it generated $33.24 billion in revenue for the nine months ended Sept. 30, up a staggering 1,200% from the same period last year. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei co-founded the company in 2021 after he and a small group of researchers defected from OpenAI , now its chief rival. Anthropic has faced sharp criticism over its positions on safety, regulation and national security, including by President Donald Trump and other senior government officials. Highlights so far: Ashton Kutcher congratulates the AI lab Market cap tops $2 trillion in debut, putting it among the tech titans ANT stock pops in first trade Protesters gather outside the Nasdaq Daniela Amodei gives a shoutout to mom Dario Amodei addresses debt and landing an investment-grade credit rating Spotted: Executives sporting "Clawd" pins at Nasdaq Dario Amodei renews pledge to pace frontier AI development Retail demand for ANT was the largest in history Anthropic employees set to get rich CNBC's reporters are covering Anthropic's IPO live on air and online from our bureaus in San Francisco and Englewood Cliffs, New Jersey, and from the Nasdaq in New York City. headlines.article_text: Stocks moving the most today: Live updates Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Dado Ruvic | Reuters In after hours Thursday, shares of Anthropic took a breather following their long-awaited debut on the market. The stock ended the regular session up 17%, but the rally failed to reignite the artificial intelligence trade. Intuit, the maker of TurboTax software, declined after its current quarter missed expectations. Follow along as CNBC covers the biggest stock market moves of the day. 1 Hour Ago Anthropic trades lower in after hours following its debut The company behind Claude saw shares slip 2% in extended trading. Anthropic in Thursday's trading Anthropic debuted on Thursday, closing 17% higher on the day. Though the company is the first pure-play AI company to come to market, the novelty wasn't enough to lift the market and the stocks in the AI trade. The Nasdaq Composite ended the day down more than 2%. -- Darla Mercado 1 Hour Ago Ross Stores' current-quarter projections miss expectations Ross Stores fell 7% as the discount retailer's forecast disappointed traders. Ross Stores on Thursday The company sees fourth-quarter earnings in a range of $2.16 to $2.25 a share, while analysts polled by LSEG sought $2.28 per share. Same-store sales for the period are also expected to rise 4% to 5%, compared to the StreetAccount consensus call for 5.1%. -- Darla Mercado 1 Hour Ago Gap ticks higher on earnings beat, but revenue misses the mark The company behind Old Navy and Banana Republic inched up 1% after third-quarter earnings surpassed expectations. Gap earned 82 cents a share on an adjusted basis, beating the LSEG consensus estimate of 78 cents. Revenue, however, fell short, coming in at $4.01 billion versus the $4.02 billion analysts were looking for. The company also announced that Ashley Kechter will be the new CEO of its Athleta brand starting next month. Athleta's prior CEO, Maggie Gauger, left to join Lululemon. -- Darla Mercado 1 Hour Ago Elastic N.V. slides after weak forecast overshadows earnings beat The data analytics company slipped 8% after its third-quarter earnings and revenue forecasts fell short of expectations. Elastic is calling for adjusted earnings in a range of 90 cents to 92 cents a share, missing the LSEG consensus estimate of 95 cents. The revenue forecast for $507.5 million to $508.5 million also fell short of the anticipated $518 million. Elastic on Thursday Second quarter adjusted earnings of 94 cents a share beat the LSEG consensus estimate of 81 cents per share. — Darla Mercado 2 Hours Ago Intuit shares drop after current-quarter guidance fails to impress Shares of the TurboTax parent tumbled 13% in extended trading after the company's second-quarter earnings projections missed estimates. Intuit on Thursday Intuit sees adjusted earnings in a range of $3.17 to $3.22 per share, while analysts polled by FactSet were looking for $3.73 per share. Separately, Intuit's first-quarter results surpassed estimates on the top and bottom lines. — Darla Mercado 5 Hours Ago NetEase shares slip after third-quarter earnings Shares of NetEase slid almost 9% after the gaming company reported weaker-than-expected earnings. NTES on Thursday The company reported 14.21 yuan in adjusted earnings per American depositary share and 27.85 billion yuan in net revenue. Analysts polled by FactSet expected 16.32 yuan in adjusted earnings per American depositary share and 30.22 billion yuan net revenue for the third quarter. — Ananya Chetia 5 Hours Ago B.Riley upgrades AST SpaceMobile to buy from neutral Shares for AST SpaceMobile popped 3% after B.Riley upgraded the company to buy from neutral. This comes despite a 60% drop in the company's shares in the last three months. ASTS The firm maintained AST SpaceMobile's price target at $48, implying nearly 90% upside from Wednesday's close. — Ananya Chetia, Nick Wells 5 Hours Ago Shares of Temu parent company surge after solid third quarter earnings U.S. traded shares of PDD Holdings rallied more than 12% in Thursday's midday trading to around $87 per share. PDD in Thursday's trading While the company's revenue for the quarter, ended Sept. 30, was flat year over year, its third quarter adjusted operating profit topped estimates. Despite Thursday's strong stock performance, shares of PDD Holdings are still down 23% year to date. — Paulina Likos 6 Hours Ago AI-linked plays’ earlier gains unravel as broader market sells off after Anthropic’s debut A slate of stocks linked to the artificial intelligence build-out effort tumbled as the broad market dropped following Anthropic's IPO. Memory stocks Micron and Sandisk were both down more than 1% in midday trading. Neoclouds CoreWeave and Nebius lost 4% and 7% respectively. Photonics company Lumentum slid 3%. Williams-Sonoma saw its comparable sales rise 5.1%, while analysts polled by FactSet sought 5.6%. Williams-Sonoma on Thursday The company also reiterated its guidance for the full year unchanged, calling for annual net revenue to grow 4.7% to 7.2%, with same-store sales in a range of 4% to 6.5%. — Darla Mercado, Nick Wells 6 Hours Ago Anthropic surges on first day of trading Anthropic shares were up 27% at around $105 on their first day of trading. headlines.article_text: Intuit to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for $3.68 billion Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Intuit has agreed to sell its Mailchimp unit to Berkshire Hathaway-backed technology firm Bending Spoons for $3.68 billion. The deal, set to close in early 2027, is less than one-third of the $12 billion Intuit paid to buy Mailchimp in 2021. In this article INTU Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT The logo of the Italian technology company Bending Spoons SpA is pictured on the facade of the company's headquarters on November 16, 2026 in Milan, Italy. Emanuele Cremaschi | Getty Images Tax software maker Intuit said Thursday that it has agreed to sell marketing subsidiary Mailchimp to Italian technology consolidator Bending Spoons for $3.68 billion in cash and stock. The deal is set to close in early 2027, according to a statement . The sale is a costly retreat for Intuit, which paid $12 billion for Mailchimp in 2021 in a push beyond its core tax and accounting businesses. Five years later, the software maker is unloading the email-marketing company for less than one-third of that price after Mailchimp became a drag on its overall revenue growth. The deal is the latest instance of Bending Spoons picking up a once promising technology asset. The company bought productivity software startup Airtable in September for 10% of what it was once worth. The Bending Spoons portfolio also contains AOL, Brightcove, Eventbrite, Evernote, Meetup, Vimeo, and WeTransfer. In August Intuit started running Mailchimp as a distinct operating segment . The move was meant to give investors more transparency as the company tried to manage the unit for profitability, Sandeep Aujla, Intuit's finance chief, said at a September company briefing. Also on Thursday, Intuit announced stronger-than-expected earnings and revenue for its fiscal first quarter, which ended on Oct. 31. The company reported $2.91 in adjusted earnings per share on $4.35 billion in revenue. Analysts polled by LSEG were looking for $2.70 per share and $4.31 billion in revenue. While Intuit's revenue increased 12% year over year, Mailchimp revenue declined 1% to $313 million. Analysts polled by StreetAccount had expected $314.4 million. Management called for $22.88 to $23.12 in adjusted earnings per share for the 2027 fiscal year, with $23.081 billion to $23.365 billion in revenue. Analysts polled by LSEG had predicted $23.62 in adjusted earnings per share on $23.43 billion in revenue. Intuit shares tumbled 15% in extended trading. The company said Mailchimp should produce $1.256 billion to $1.266 billion in fiscal 2027 revenue, which would be down 1% to flat year over year. In August Aujla said Intuit anticipated Mailchimp's higher effective prices offsetting increased client churn. Mailchimp was founded in 2001. Rivals include Klaviyo , which went public in 2023. Berkshire Hathaway invested $600 million in Bending Spoons when the acquirer went public in July, and in October Bending Spoons said Berkshire invested another $330 million .
